answer: Each identity locks a 60-credit violet bond and declares one spiral route through distinct checkpoints. Each epoch it must wander the route, collecting one key-signed violet stamp per checkpoint. Auditors replay the spiral ledger; any missing, out-of-order, or reused stamp burns the bond. First route: 25 in fees. The k-th fake takes a longer outward spiral leg, paying 25+3(k-1) (1,000th: 3,022 plus 60 at risk); 1,000 fakes pay 1,523,500 in fees, 60,000 bonded. A rented-route ring fails: stamps bind to one key. An honest identity pays 60 once plus 25 and keeps its bond after a clean epoch.
